{{Quote|You're leading a battle-hardened unit, supported by ''Juggernauts, commandos'' and two ''Jedi''!|[[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]], to [[Rex/Legends|Rex]]|<ref name="Burn the Behemoth!">{{TCWComicCite|6.17|Burn the Behemoth!}}</ref>}}
The '''HAVw A6 Juggernaut''', also known as the '''A6 Juggernaut''', '''Clone turbo tank''', or '''HAVw A6 heavy assault vehicle''', was an upgraded version of the [[HAVw A5 Juggernaut]].

==Description==
{{Quote|<nowiki />''Zone runners'', sir! They're in amongst the Juggernauts!|A stormtrooper, on [[zone runner]]s|<ref name="Rebellion 6">[[Rebellion 6|''Rebellion'' 6]]</ref>}}
[[File:HAVw-A6Juggernaut-SWTCG.png|thumb|left|200px|The A6 Juggernaut was larger than previous models.]]
The A6 Juggernaut model was larger than its predecessor. It measured 30.4 meters in height and 49.4 meters in length. Its interior space was greatly increased to allow for up to three hundred troopers and equipment, a complement of close support craft such as [[Speeder bike/Legends|speeder bikes]] and light [[Airspeeder/Legends|airspeeders]], or a mix of both. A combination of twelve crew members were required to pilot and control the massive vehicle, although with an automation package, that requirement could be reduced to just two pilots.

With thick, thermally superconducting armor (capable of absorbing enemy fire and dispersing heat over a wide area) and a heavier load, the A6 Juggernaut could only achieve 160 kilometers per hour, and the turning issues of the A5 model were magnified with the A6. The slowness required for negotiating turns encouraged the A6's use on open terrain rather than urban battlefields.

<div style="float:right">[[File:Juggernaut_ICS.jpg|thumb|left|200px|An A6 Juggernaut cross-section.]]</div>
Weapons systems were also upgraded to include a heavy [[Laser cannon/Legends|laser cannon]] turret, a rapid repeating laser cannon, two medium antipersonnel laser cannons, two twin antipersonnel [[Blaster cannon/Legends|blaster cannons]], and two turreted projectile launchers, loadable with variable-yield [[Concussion grenade/Legends|concussion grenades]] for close support or missiles added for anti-armor firepower. Missile range was 30km. Against an unshielded target, a Juggernaut could deliver the heat of a [[Nuclear weapon/Legends|nuclear bomb]] into a small area.<ref name="Revenge of the Sith: Incredible Cross-Sections">''[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith Incredible Cross-Sections]]''</ref>

From a small pod above the vehicle's front, a spotter kept lookout for enemy forces. Though there was a large view of the area, he was an easy target for hostile troops. This observation mast could be retracted when not in use.

==History==
{{Quote|Imperial Juggernaughts. ''[sic]'' More of them.|[[Ved Tarson]], to [[Wyl Tarson]]|<ref name="Rebellion 8">[[Rebellion 8|''Rebellion'' 8]]</ref>}}
The A6 model saw its heaviest use in service of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]. Due to a flawed direct-delivery system maintained by [[Kuat Drive Yards/Legends|Kuat Drive Yards]] during the conflict, some A6 Juggernauts also fell into the hands of the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|CIS]].
[[File:JuggernautROTS.jpg|thumb|left|200px|A6 Juggernaut launching missiles during the Battle of Kashyyyk.]]
HAVw A6 Juggernauts were used fairly extensively in the [[Battle of Kashyyyk/Legends|Battle of Kashyyyk]] alongside [[All Terrain Attack Pod/Legends|AT-APs]], where they went up against enemy [[NR-N99 Persuader-class droid enforcer/Legends|NR-N99 tank droids]] and [[DSD1 dwarf spider droid/Legends|DSD1 dwarf spider droids]].

After the Clone Wars, the [[Imperial Army/Legends|Imperial Army]] developed sleeker and more versatile combat vehicles. The various Juggernaut models were gradually phased out, and during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], they primarily served on battlefronts in the Outer Rim. Some fell into the hands of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]]. According to Imperial-turned Rebel General [[Crix Madine/Legends|Crix Madine]], the HAVw A6 Juggernauts tended to break down.<ref name="IHB">''[[Star Wars: Imperial Handbook: A Commander's Guide]]''</ref> It appears that the [[HAVt B5 Juggernaut]] served as its successor, even though its purpose was different. A6s were deployed in the [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|Battle of Hoth]]. By [[13 ABY/Legends|13 ABY]], they were one of a number of Clone Wars-era Galactic Republic vehicles being used by the [[Restored Empire]] faction of the [[Imperial Remnant/Legends|Imperial Remnant]].<ref name="CE3">[[Crimson Empire III: Empire Lost 2|''Crimson Empire III: Empire Lost'' 2]]</ref>

Later-generation [[All Terrain Armored Transport/Legends|AT-ATs]] would borrow certain design-elements from the Juggernauts.

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:NewPlymptoJuggernaut.jpg|thumb|right|200px|A6 Juggernauts deployed on [[New Plympto/Legends|New Plympto]].]]
The Juggernaut's designs entered the [[Star Wars Legends|Expanded Universe]] via [[Joe Johnston]]'s sketches of an unused heavy assault vehicle intended for [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|''The Empire Strikes Back'']]. It and its role in the film was replaced by the AT-AT.

When chosen to appear in ''Revenge of the Sith'', the realization of its scale and weapon systems greatly outstripped those imagined by the Expanded Universe, being roughly larger by a scale factor of two, or eight times larger in volume. To accommodate this, the version that appears on-screen was denoted as the A6 model, with the smaller, EU model already denoted as the A5.

[[File:HAVwA6Juggernaut-FFp41.png|thumb|left|200px|The HAVw A6 Juggernaut (28.51 meters long) variant<ref name=":0">''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: Incredible Vehicles]] (p. 23)''</ref> seen in [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars|''The Clone Wars'']] series]]
In ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' there is an sub-variant of the the A6 Juggernaut, being significantly smaller compared to its much larger counterpart that appeared in ''Revenge of the Sith,'' as it is often similar in size to [[All Terrain Tactical Enforcer/Legends|AT-TEs]].<ref name="Holocron Heist">{{TCW|Holocron Heist}}</ref> The Havw A6 Juggernaut is 49.4 meters long,<ref name="Revenge of the Sith: Incredible Cross-Sections" /> however; in the Clone Wars series, it is 28.51 meters long.<ref name="Incredible Vehicles">''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: Incredible Vehicles]]''</ref> This smaller version used in the series, despite being classified as the A6 model, has key visual differences other than its size such as its hatches that feature mounted [[Heavy repeating blaster/Legends|heavy repeating blasters]] instead of dome turret canons and a lack of an extendable observation pod.<ref name="Incredible Vehicles" /><ref name="Holocron Heist" />

[[File:HavwA6_Juggernaut_TCW.png|thumb|right|200px|First Battle of Felucia (28.51 meters long) variant<ref name=":0" />]]
The "Clone Turbo Tank" name possibly arose because at the time of the release of the prequels, Toy Biz owned the rights to produce toys named "Juggernaut" (as they had the Marvel license). Though Hasbro now has the rights to this name, the 2009 toy was still named Clone Turbo Tank. [[The LEGO Group]] has also made 3 models of a Juggernaut, all called "Clone Turbo Tank". The first Clone Turbo Tank Lego set 7261, released in 2005, is an A6 Juggernaut model, as seen in ''Revenge of the Sith'' during the Battle of Kashyyyk. The second set 8098, released in August 2010, is a Juggernaut model with specifications similar to that of an A5 Juggernaut, as seen in the ''Clone Wars'' series during the Battle of Felucia. The third set 75151, released in May 2016, is based on the A6 Juggernaut from ''Revenge of the Sith ''during the Battle of Kashyyyk, similar to the first model.
